newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA'S ECONOMY DOWN 2.0 PCT IN 1997-PM.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA'S ECONOMY DOWN 2.0 PCT IN 1997-PM.

text.p: Romania's gross domestic product (GDP) is expected to fall by around 2.0 percent in real terms this year, after a 4.1 percent growth in 1996, Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea said on Monday.

"Although the real gross domestic product will slide by 2.0 percent,...owing especially to the solid results of small but dynamic companies, we expect economic growth to resume in 1998," Ciorbea told a news conference announcing the reform package following loan talks with the International Monetary Fund and World Bank.
Romania is seeking around $1.0 billion in total loans from the IMF and the World Bank to push through with reform drive.
Both lenders had withheld credits to Romania last year over foreign exchange market curbs and overspending by the former ruling leftists in an election year.

Year-on-year inflation, which surged to 56.9 percent in 1996 -- more than triple the target agreed with the Fund -- was forecast to soar to 97.0 percent this year, led by January's fuel price hike and planned electricity and food price rises.
But Ciorbea said that inflation would slow down in the last months of 1997, to an annualised rate of some 30 percent, as a result of tight monetary and fiancial policies.

Romania's economy expanded by 7.1 percent in 1995, up from 3.9 in the previous year. But that growth was "unsound" and led by import-driven policies, which Ciorbea's centrist coalition has vowed to reverse. ($6,822 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
